newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom says no assets frozen.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom says no assets frozen.

text.p: A spokesman for RAO Gazprom said on Monday it was impossible for assets of the Russian gas monopoly to be frozen without disrupting gas supplies, and therefore reports that assets of its subsidiaries had been frozen were not true.

The spokesman said a claim that assets had been frozen in a letter to deputies from Gazprom chairman Rem Vyakhirev should not be taken literally but was intended to "increase influence on those who think".
"The main thing this letter was aiming for was for the consumers of our gas to pay their debts," deputy spokesman Anatoly Kotov told Reuters.

Prime-Tass news agency said on Monday that tax authorities in the Perm region and Komi Republic had frozen the accounts of two Gazprom subsidiaries which owe the federal and regional authorities around 1 trillion roubles ($184.5 million) in back taxes.

Kotov confirmed that the two subsidiaries, and three other subsidiaries whose assets have been reported to be frozen, owed large amounts of back taxes to the federal and local governments but said he was unable to confirm that their assets had been frozen.
"If they stop working, then gas won't come from the North to Moscow and to (Western) Europe, because it goes through one pipe. It would be a crime if they stopped working," he said.
Because of this, sanctions such as freezing accounts had never been applied to companies transporting gas, he said.
Vyakhirev said in a letter to parliament last week that the government had frozen the accounts of Gazprom's major production unit to rake back tax arrears.
Gazprom admits it owes more than 15 trillion roubles in back taxes but says it is owed more than three times that amount by consumers, including the government.
The report of the latest asset-freezing coincided with the long-awaited details of Gazprom's international share offering.

Lead managers of the offering for Gazprom, the world's biggest gas company, said on Monday the preliminary price for an American Depositary Share would be between $14 and $16. Each ADS represents 10 oridnary shares.
